_comment: ADR-037 register fragment — rule nested-auth write-only path (ocon#147 LAST residual, adopting openregister#459/#463). SECURITY FIX. An `authentication`-type rule stores its inbound API keys at `configuration.authentication.keys` — a map of apiKey => nextcloud userId (see src/modals/Rule/EditRule.vue). A caller presenting one of those keys is authenticated AS that mapped user, so the map is a set of live impersonation credentials. 99-rule-lockdown.json (ocon#147 phase C) closed the disclosure to NON-admins by making every verb admin-only, but it explicitly left a residual: an admin could still read the keys via the generic OpenRegister API, because the secret lives NESTED under the untyped `configuration` object and OpenRegister resolved writeOnly from TOP-LEVEL schema properties only — a marker nested at `configuration.authentication.keys` stripped nothing, and blanket-writeOnly on `configuration` breaks the editor (it reads the whole configuration back to populate every action form). openregister#459 added the missing declaration surface: `x-openregister-writeonly-paths`, a schema-level annotation listing dot-paths from the object root. A declared path AND its whole sub-tree are stripped on EVERY rendered read — unconditionally, admins included, list/search included (openregister#460/#462), plus the `@self.relations` mirror where SaveObject::scanForRelations flattens nested values into literal dot-path keys (this is what covers `configuration.authentication.keys.<apiKey>`, whose leaf segments are operator-supplied and cannot be enumerated in advance). THE ENGINE STILL SEES THE KEYS: EndpointService::getRuleById() now re-reads the rule with `_render: false` (EndpointService.php ~L2769) BEFORE processAuthenticationRule() touches the keys — `_render: false` is the load-bearing argument, NOT `_rbac: false` (the strip is SCHEMA-gated at RenderObject::schemaHasWriteOnlyRule, so an `_rbac: false` read still loses the value; that was the ocon#212/#226 lesson). WHY THE FRONTEND MUST OMIT ON SAVE: the write-only read strip means the rule editor never receives the stored keys, so its apiKeys UI seeds empty. openregister#463 (save-side write-only preserve) carries an OMITTED write-only value forward from the stored object, so EditRule.vue omits `configuration.authentication.keys` entirely whenever the operator entered no complete new key (buildAuthenticationConfiguration.js) — sending `keys: []` would instead let OpenRegister's PUT-semantic null-fill DESTROY every stored key. DELIBERATELY NOT MARKED: `type`/`users`/`groups` are non-secret authentication settings the editor must read back to populate the form. A malformed path, or a root segment naming an undeclared property, ABORTS the save (openregister#459 deliberately exempts this annotation from openregister#419's drop-the-bad-key isolation — silent degradation on a security annotation is fail-open); `configuration` is a declared top-level property of `rule`, so this path is well-rooted. Version bumped 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0: OpenRegister re-imports a schema only when the incoming version exceeds the stored one, so a content change without a bump is a silent no-op on existing installs.
